title: American Photographs
subtitle: Famous images from the Library of Congress collections, 1863–1943
intro:
Eleven photographs held by or associated with the **Library of Congress**: Civil War views, portraits of Lincoln, Douglass and Tubman, the first powered flight, Lewis Hine's child labour reports and the Farm Security Administration's record of the Depression.

The originals are mostly small negatives and prints. Here they hang as large exhibition prints. Each label gives the medium of the original. All images are public domain or have no known restrictions; files come from Wikimedia Commons copies of the LoC and museum scans.

artworks.title: Destitute pea pickers in California. Mother of seven children. Age thirty-two. Nipomo, California ("Migrant Mother")
artworks.medium: Nitrate film negative, 4 × 5 in.; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection
artworks.credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection

provenance.event: Made by Lange for the Resettlement Administration (later Farm Security Administration) at a pea pickers' camp in Nipomo
Published in the San Francisco News, prompting federal food aid to the camp
FSA/OWI photographic file transferred to the Library of Congress
The thumb in the lower right corner of the negative was retouched out of later prints

artworks.rights: No known restrictions on publication (Library of Congress)
artworks.description: Florence Owens Thompson and her children, photographed in a few exposures as Lange was driving home. The image became the defining picture of the Depression. Thompson's identity was not made public until the 1970s.

artworks.title: Farmer and sons walking in the face of a dust storm. Cimarron County, Oklahoma
artworks.medium: Film negative; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection
artworks.credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection

provenance.event: Made for the Resettlement Administration during Rothstein's assignment in the Dust Bowl
FSA/OWI file transferred to the Library of Congress

artworks.description: Farmer Arthur Coble and his sons head for shelter on their land near Boise City. It became the best-known image of the Dust Bowl.

artworks.title: Allie Mae Burroughs, wife of a cotton sharecropper, Hale County, Alabama
artworks.medium: Film negative, 8 × 10 in.; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection
artworks.credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection

provenance.event: Made while Evans was on leave from the FSA, working with the writer James Agee
Published in Let Us Now Praise Famous Men
FSA/OWI file transferred to the Library of Congress

artworks.title: Washington, D.C. Government charwoman ("American Gothic")
artworks.medium: Film negative; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection
artworks.credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, FSA/OWI Collection

provenance.event: Made by Parks in his first weeks as an FSA photographer
FSA/OWI file transferred to the Library of Congress

artworks.description: Ella Watson, who cleaned the FSA building, posed with her mop and broom before the flag, in a pointed echo of Grant Wood's *American Gothic*. Parks's FSA chief Roy Stryker thought it too provocative to publish at the time.

artworks.title: Abraham Lincoln
artworks.medium: Albumen print from wet collodion negative; shown enlarged
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division

provenance.event: Made at Gardner's gallery in Washington, eleven days before the Gettysburg Address
Prints in the Library of Congress and other collections

artworks.title: Frederick Douglass, head-and-shoulders portrait, facing right
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division

provenance.event: Douglass sat for more photographs than any other American of the 19th century, using portraits to counter racist caricature
Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division

artworks.title: Harriet Tubman
artworks.medium: Albumen print on carte-de-visite mount; shown enlarged
artworks.collection: Library of Congress and Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture

provenance.event: Made by Powelson in Auburn, New York, where Tubman lived after the Civil War
Kept in a photograph album of the Quaker abolitionist and teacher Emily Howland
Album bought jointly at auction by the Library of Congress and the NMAAHC

artworks.description: The earliest known photograph of Tubman, taken a few years after the war in which she served as a scout, spy and nurse for the Union army.

artworks.title: First flight, 120 feet in 12 seconds, 10:35 a.m.; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina
artworks.medium: Glass plate negative; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, Wright Brothers Negatives

provenance.event: Exposed by Daniels, a member of the Kill Devil Hills lifesaving station, on Orville Wright's camera
Plate damaged in the Dayton flood; Wright family collection
Wright brothers' negatives donated to the Library of Congress by the Wright estate

artworks.rights: No known restrictions on publication (Library of Congress)
artworks.description: Orville Wright at the controls; Wilbur runs alongside. Daniels had never used a camera before. It is the only photograph of the first powered, controlled flight.

artworks.title: Addie Card, 12 years. Spinner in North Pownal Cotton Mill, Vermont
artworks.medium: Glass negative; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, National Child Labor Committee Collection

provenance.event: Made for the National Child Labor Committee's investigation of mill work
NCLC photographs and records given to the Library of Congress

artworks.rights: No known restrictions on publication (Library of Congress)
artworks.description: Hine's captions record that the girls in the mill said Addie was ten. His photographs helped bring about federal child labour laws.

artworks.title: Farm workers, Mt. Williamson in background, Manzanar Relocation Center
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver negative; shown as an exhibition print
artworks.collection: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, Ansel Adams's Photographs of Japanese-American Internment at Manzanar

provenance.event: Made by Adams during visits to the Manzanar War Relocation Center, California
Adams gave the Manzanar photographs and negatives to the Library of Congress

artworks.rights: No known restrictions on publication (Library of Congress)

artworks.title: A Harvest of Death, Gettysburg, July 1863
artworks.medium: Albumen print from glass negative; plate 36 of Gardner's Photographic Sketch Book of the War
artworks.collection: Library of Congress holds copies of Gardner's Sketch Book; this scan: Google Art Project

provenance.event: Photographed on the battlefield at Gettysburg by O'Sullivan, working for Alexander Gardner
Published by Gardner as plate 36 of the Photographic Sketch Book of the War
